notes: Derived edit (ABox), re-picked by the round-2 verifier: the earlier 0016 (SN 1987A in the Local Group -> the Virgo Cluster) had a w2 that moved the Large Magellanic Cloud, with the Small Magellanic Cloud, the Magellanic Stream and its satellite orbit around the Milky Way, into a cluster 54 million light-years away, contradicting firm facts about other things (the Milky Way's satellites, the SMC, a naked-eye cloud 10° across); with only w1 left the premises were over-determined. The original follows from two located_in facts by transitivity; Q1 is the premise route ('the galaxy in which SN 2011fe occurred'); Q2 applies transitivity once more to the new value (bridge: Sculptor is wholly southern), and the edit crosses from a northern-sky galaxy (declination about +54°) into a wholly southern constellation, so it discriminates. Worlds: w1 the supernova's galaxy gives way, w2 the Pinwheel Galaxy's constellation. Constellation membership is a matter of IAU boundaries, so neither world breaks a physical law or a fact about another named place: Sculptor (declination −25° to −39°) contains the south galactic pole, so a galaxy there is unobscured, and it is observable from Palomar, where PTF found the supernova. Derivability likely: 0 exact direct hits, 29 co-occurrences with Ursa Major against 667 with M101. R2: neither SN 2011fe nor its zh/es names name a constellation; the Chinese 玉夫座 / 大熊座 are the standard names. Near query (SN 1987A, the Large Magellanic Cloud) is not a premise and differs from the new value. Since 2026-10-31 (formal check, FINDINGS C2 and E) the worlds name the premise that gives way and its side facts rather than the answer: w1's galaxy is 'some other galaxy' and w2's constellation 'some other constellation', and the answers follow through transitivity and one constellation per object, now a step of the chains; w2 lists the Pinwheel Galaxy's place in the northern celestial hemisphere among its side facts (q1's original 'no' rests on it).
